crossRefs.note: For of the wise man, even as of the fool, there is no memory forever, since in the days to come all will have been long…
But man, despite his riches, doesn’t endure. He is like the animals that perish.
A man who has riches without understanding, is like the animals that perish.
A senseless man doesn’t know, neither does a fool understand this:
though the wicked spring up as the grass, and all the evildoers flourish, they will be destroyed forever.
For we must die, and are like water spilled on the ground, which can’t be gathered up again; neither does God take away…
But man dies, and is laid low. Yes, man gives up the spirit, and where is he?
You hide your face; they are troubled. You take away their breath; they die and return to the dust.
Therefore I began to cause my heart to despair concerning all the labor in which I had labored under the sun.
Behold, you have made my days hand widths. My lifetime is as nothing before you. Surely every man stands as a breath.”
“Surely every man walks like a shadow. Surely they busy themselves in vain. He heaps up, and doesn’t know who shall…
Remember how short my time is, for what vanity you have created all the children of men!
What man is he who shall live and not see death, who shall deliver his soul from the power of Sheol?

translations.web: For that which happens to the sons of men happens to animals. Even one thing happens to them. As the one dies, so the other dies. Yes, they have all one breath; and man has no advantage over the animals; for all is vanity.
translations.bsb: For the fates of both men and beasts are the same: As one dies, so dies the other—they all have the same breath. Man has no advantage over the animals, since everything is futile.
translations.kjv: For that which befalleth the sons of men befalleth beasts; even one thing befalleth them: as the one dieth, so dieth the other; yea, they have all one breath; so that a man hath no preeminence above a beast: for all is vanity.
translations.asv: For that which befalleth the sons of men befalleth beasts; even one thing befalleth them: as the one dieth, so dieth the other; yea, they have all one breath; and man hath no preeminence above the beasts: for all is vanity.
